reaction.episode: The current episode is DIGESTION through October 28, not capitulation: SPX at 7743.98 is only 1.28% below its 120-day high, 0.6% above its 50-day (7698.05) and 6.04% above its 200-day (7302.71), while SMH (567.67, above Zone 1) and NVDA (215.38, above Zone 1) have not entered their buy zones, VIX is 16.91, HY OAS is 3.23% and calm, and the mechanical capitulation tally is just 1 of 4 (credit calm only). Episode data is fresh, not stale.
reaction.invalidation: A SPX close below its 50-day average (7698.05) combined with HY OAS breaking above 4% would prove the Watch stance wrong by converting DIGESTION into a credit-led rollover and voiding this ladder; conversely, a held close above SMH 600 / SPX 7820 on rising volume would prove Watch too cautious and mark the digestion as continuation, not a top.

ladder.response: Probe only: small starter positions in the highest-conviction dislocations (AVGO, ONTO) at no more than probe size, with the rest of the ladder held back until capitulation confirms
ladder.trigger: SMH prints inside Zone 1 (540-565) or NVDA inside Zone 1 (200-210), with the tally still below 3

ladder.response: Fire Tranche A (25% of new money) into the zone names per the approved deployment ladder; do not deploy the remaining tranches on this print alone
ladder.trigger: Escalation: SMH prints inside Zone 2 (470-505) or NVDA inside Zone 2 (175-185) AND the mechanical tally reaches 3 or more

ladder.response: Do not chase the first bounce and do not add: hold existing probes, wait for the failure-zone retest verdict, and only add on a confirmed second low holding above the zone lows
ladder.trigger: Trap case: a bounce carries SMH into the 580-600 failure zone or SPX into 7750-7820 and fails there

ladder.response: Stand down: void this ladder, freeze new probes, and move the portfolio stance to Hold/Trim until credit calms and a new episode state prints
ladder.trigger: Stand-down / regime break: HY OAS above 4% or VIX above 25, or SPX closing below its 50-day (7698.05) with credit cracking

ladder.response: Re-enter per the confirmed-bottom condition: scale into the probe list on the second low holding, with size gated by whether the failure zone is reclaimed and held
ladder.trigger: Re-entry: a failed first bounce followed by a second low holding with the 10-year falling, or a held close above SPX 7750-7820 / SMH 580-600

reaction.trapRisk: The pivot-and-fail scenario is the central trap risk in DIGESTION: the first bounce toward SMH 580-600 / SPX 7750-7820 looks like resumption but is the failure zone by construction, so entries must not chase it — wait for the retest verdict, require a second low to hold, and treat any probe added into the bounce as a trade to be cut, not a position to be averaged, if the failure zone rejects price.

strategyPosture: Watch, with a loaded probe list: the tape is digesting, not capitulating — SMH and NVDA sit above their buy zones, the mechanical capitulation tally is only 1 of 4, and credit is calm — so no tranche fires today, but AVGO, ONTO, NXT and LRCX are the names to buy on zone prints, not on bounces.

themes.counterRead: Index-level calm (SPY only 0.67% down on the day, SPX 1.28% off its 120-day high) masks real damage in the names that dominate index weight, weakest GOOGL at 30.9% below its high. Positioning off the index alone understates the drawdown in the leadership complex; the risk to watch is credit flipping, which would convert rotation into rollover.
themes.dataAnchor: The weakness is concentrated, not broad: Mag7 names average 14.46% below their 52-week highs versus SPY only 1.8% below its high, a 12.66-point divergence gap, while IWM rose 0.76% on the day and 2.0% over the month against QQQ's 3.64% monthly fall. Credit confirms the rotation read rather than a rollover: bank lending standards are LOOSE at a 0% SLOOS reading, far below the ~40% stress threshold, and HY OAS sits at 3.23%.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover: mega-cap weakness against a calm tape
themes.narrative: The tape reads like a broad selloff when the mega-cap names lead lower, with QQQ down 1.76% on the day and 3.64% over the month.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS breaking above 4% or SLOOS moving toward the 40% stress threshold would void the rotation read.

themes.counterRead: Revenue and cash generation are moving opposite to price across the complex, which is the classic DATA_AHEAD setup — but dislocation alone is not a buy signal: SMH at 567.67 and NVDA at 215.38 both sit ABOVE their Zone 1 buy zones (SMH 540-565, NVDA 200-210), so the entry trigger has not printed. The opportunity is a watchlist to be bought on zone occupancy, not chased mid-digestion.
themes.dataAnchor: The dislocation list shows 29 names, heavily semiconductor-weighted: AVGO sits 30.4% below its high while revenue grows 55% year over year with a 67.8% gross margin and 42.1% FCF margin; ONTO is 42.3% below its high on 22.1% revenue growth; LRCX is 42% below its high on 131.3% revenue growth; MU is 25.7% below its high. SMH itself is 15.5% off its 120-day high yet still 9.59% above its 200-day average, and NVDA is 11.5% off its high and 5.51% above its 200-day.
themes.label: AI semiconductor dislocation: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The market narrative treats the AI hardware complex as played out, pricing semis as if the capex cycle has already peaked.
themes.watchFor: SMH printing inside 540-565 or NVDA inside 200-210 would activate the probe rung of the ladder.

themes.counterRead: VST's own revenue inflection reads DETERIORATING even as the headline growth number holds up, so the power theme is not uniformly clean — NXT's recovery inflection is the stronger leg. The divergence argues for ranking NXT ahead of VST and sizing any power probe on the revenue-inflection verdict, not the theme label.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is 29% below its high on 19.1% revenue growth and a 2.7x price-to-sales multiple, and insiders bought $1.17M at the trough. NXT is 51% below its peak with revenue growing 31.6% year over year and a recovery-confirmed inflection. Both screen as watchlist promotions at score 78, the joint-highest watchlist scores in the input.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power: trough pricing with insider confirmation
themes.narrative: Power names tied to the AI buildout are treated as yesterday's theme, left behind as attention rotated elsewhere.
themes.watchFor: VST's revenue inflection flipping from DETERIORATING to RECOVERY, or NXT holding above its trough on a retest, would strengthen the power probe case.

themes.counterRead: An RSI of 22 after a 13% single-day fall is a snapback setup, not a value verdict: the input carries no GOOGL fundamental anchor to say the new price is cheap, only that the old price assumed too much. Catching this knife before the catalyst is digested mistakes oversold for undervalued; the disciplined read is to let GOOGL find a level and confirm, while treating it as the weakest Mag7 name dragging the concentration gap wider.
themes.dataAnchor: GOOGL fell 12.96% on the day and is down 17.81% over the month, now 30.9% below its 52-week high with an RSI of 22 — the deepest oversold reading in the dislocation list — and its decline reason is coded ACUTE_CATALYST rather than the SENTIMENT_DRIVEN tag carried by most dislocations. META shows the other side of the same reset: down 13.65% over the month but up 2.24% on the day, a two-way tape inside the same complex.
themes.label: GOOGL's acute break: the perfection premium unwinding
themes.narrative: Mega-cap AI leaders were priced as if flawless execution were guaranteed, so any crack in the story reprices violently.
themes.watchFor: GOOGL stabilizing with RSI recovering above 30 on a higher low, or a further leg taking the Mag7 average gap past 15 points, would change this read.

themes.counterRead: A 10-year near 5% with a positively sloped curve is restrictive enough to cap multiple expansion even without a credit event — the tape does not need a crisis to stay in digestion. The FOMC event's HIGH signal strength with no beneficiary names attached in the input means the rate path, not any sector bet, is the swing factor into December.
themes.dataAnchor: The rate stack matches that narrative: fed funds at 3.88%, the 2-year at 4.77%, the 10-year at 4.99% and the 30-year at 5.34%, a 2s10s curve of +0.22 and a real 10-year of 2.64%. Credit is not confirming stress: HY OAS is 3.23% and the episode block flags credit as calm and not cracking, while VIX sits at 16.6-16.91, well below the 25 stand-down line.
themes.label: Rates and the FOMC: tight money, calm credit
themes.narrative: With the October 27-28 FOMC decision as the active HIGH-signal event and the December 8-9 meeting already anticipated at HIGH signal, the market is positioned for rates to stay restrictive.
themes.watchFor: The 10-year sustaining above 5.2% or HY OAS above 4% would shift this theme from ALIGNED to a regime break.
